The region shown above enclosed by the curves $y=3-x$ and $y={x}^{2}$ for $x\in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=4.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/255abcfb1a9034df297dc4939d945d8c3b1c4bd717cebde2844aa2a229fd5258.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=3-x,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y={x}^{2}.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y={x}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/4b480a3bb7312a59edcabb133100bee1ebd5777664ea490b58744171e05e3083.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(4)-({x}^{2})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[4-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=3-x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/20de93738463a5b04c0c5c0884d1db7d8867503931122c99a27fc82493b64edb.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(4)-(3-x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[1+x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[4-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[1+x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({(4-{x}^{2})}^{2}-{(1+x)}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-9{x}^{2}-2x+15)\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}-3{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+15x)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{1}{5}(1)^{5}-3(1)^{3}-(1)^{2}+15(1))-0] \\  & =\pi (\frac{1}{5}-3-1+15) \\  & =\pi (11+\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\pi (\frac{55}{5}+\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{56\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
